vignette:
Amir, a 40-year-old software engineer, sat in the therapist's office with an anxious energy that seemed to vibrate through the air. He had come to seek help after months of feeling trapped in his own mind. The traumatic event that had turned his life upside down was a devastating earthquake that struck his hometown, leaving destruction in its wake and claiming lives indiscriminately. Amir vividly recalled that day; the ground shook violently, and buildings crumbled around him. He could still hear the terrifying sounds of metal bending and glass shattering, filling his ears with echoes of chaos. It was an experience that replayed in his mind, a loop of images and sounds that he could not escape.

In the months following the earthquake, Amir struggled to make sense of his new reality. He had always prided himself on being the positive one in his family, the one who could find a silver lining in any situation. Yet, this disaster felt insurmountable. He found himself forcing positive thoughts, trying to convince himself that the future held promise. However, every time he attempted to uplift his spirits, a wave of despair would crash over him, leaving him feeling more isolated and miserable. He was haunted by the sense that he had let his family down; they relied on his optimism, and he felt he was failing them.

The memories of that fateful day intruded on his life, uninvited and relentless. When he closed his eyes, he could hear the haunting sounds—the cries of people trapped beneath rubble, the sirens wailing in the distance. These auditory memories would surface unexpectedly, and he often found himself frozen in fear, as if he were right back in that moment. Confusion plagued him, too; he struggled to put the sequence of events in order, a jumble of sights and sounds that left him disoriented and anxious. Each memory felt vividly real, flooding his senses with visceral reminders of the terror he had experienced.

As time went on, Amir noticed he was increasingly on edge. In meetings at work, he would jump at the slightest unexpected movement, his heart racing as if he were still running for his life. He became hyper-vigilant, always scanning the room for an escape route, his mind fixated on the idea that danger lurked around every corner. This heightened state of alertness led to strained interactions with colleagues, who began to notice his withdrawn demeanor. Amir felt guilty; he was aware that his behavior was affecting his work relationships, yet he couldn’t shake the underlying fear that had taken hold of him.

Amir also developed an aversion to anything remotely related to medical situations. The mere sight of an ambulance or a hospital triggered panic within him, memories of the frantic rush to save lives during the aftermath of the earthquake flooding back with alarming intensity. He would avoid any medical appointments, rationalizing that he was simply too busy at work or too focused on family obligations. This avoidance, however, accumulated over time, leading to a growing sense of neglect regarding his own health.

The weight of his negative appraisals grew unbearable. Amir often found himself reflecting on how he could have avoided the disaster. He believed he should have been more vigilant, more prepared, and that someone else would have handled the situation better. This self-comparison left him feeling trapped in a cycle of shame and guilt. He no longer saw a future that held joy, convinced that nothing good could happen to him anymore. The laughter he once shared with his wife felt distant, as if it belonged to someone else. His happiness had been replaced by a persistent cloud of misery that hung over him.

It was this accumulation of distress that finally pushed Amir to seek help. On a particularly difficult day, after a confrontation with his wife about his withdrawal and moodiness, he felt an overwhelming sense of hopelessness. He realized he could no longer continue living in this state of fear and sadness. In his mind, he clung to the hope that maybe, just maybe, therapy could help him reclaim the happiness he had lost. Yet, beneath that hope lay a deep fear—fear that he would always be trapped in this cycle of pain, unable to escape the memories that haunted him. Amir sat in the office, a mix of apprehension and hope swirling within him, yearning for a way to find peace once more.
